title: Forty Words about Notes
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：voice　|　正文 374 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 voice 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: I was the quietest student in a class that was never quiet. Our English teacher used to say that knowing a language does not mean having a ① voice, and for two years I took this to be simply how I was made. A voice, it turns out, is not a personality; it is a habit.

The turning point was small. We were asked to ② voice an opinion about a poem in front of everybody. My friend Lin said three sentences and sat down. When my turn came I found that my own ③ voice sounded strange to me, thinner than in my head, and I stopped after six words. Nobody laughed. People rarely do, and nobody had told me that.

Two things changed that year. First I learned to write before I spoke: the notes I passed to myself at break became the sentences I said after lunch. Second, I noticed that most of a discussion is listening, and that listening well gives you something real to say. When our class argued about banning phones in the library, I ④ voiced a view nobody else had offered: that the rule mattered less than the reason written beside it.

Our teacher kept one rule: nobody might ⑤ raise their voice, because shouting ends a conversation faster than silence does. She also taught us the active and passive ⑥ voice, which has nothing to do with confidence and everything to do with who does what to whom. I liked that grammar lesson better than any other; it made argument feel measurable, and a quiet voice can still be heard if the room is quiet enough.

That winter I lost my ⑦ voice twice to a cold, and both times I filled a notebook instead. In June the head teacher asked every student to speak for one minute about anything at all. I went last, ⑧ in a voice I recognised at last as my own, and said forty words about taking notes. Afterwards a girl I had never spoken to said quietly: 'Everybody here should have a ⑨ voice in decisions like this.' She was right. I have never since believed that being quiet and having nothing to say are the same thing, and everybody deserves to be heard in their own ⑩ voice.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 发言权；表达意见的机会
C. n. 心声；个人的表达方式
E. v. 表达；说出（意见、疑虑）
F. 固定搭配：in a ... voice 用……的声音
G. 固定搭配：raise one's voice 提高嗓门
H. 固定搭配：lose one's voice 失声；嗓子哑了

items.q: does not mean having a voice
to voice an opinion about a poem
my own voice sounded strange to me
I voiced a view nobody else had offered
I lost my voice twice to a cold
in a voice I recognised at last as my own
should have a voice in decisions like this

answers.why: having a voice 与 knowing a language 相对，指“有发言权、能表达自己的机会”，而非嗓音。
voice＋宾语 an opinion，是动词“表达、说出”，老师要求当众谈看法。
my own voice sounded strange 指自己的“说话声”听起来陌生，是嗓音。
voice a view 同样是动词“说出”，指在争论中提出别人没提过的看法。
raise one's voice 意为“提高嗓门”，老师规定任何人不得这样做。
active/passive voice 是语法术语“语态”，与被动语态的结构有关。
lose one's voice 意为“嗓子哑了、失声”，此处因感冒两次失声。
in a ... voice 意为“用……的声音”，此处作者终于认出那是自己的声音。
have a voice in sth 意为“在某事上有发言权”，与第 1 题同义复现。
in their own voice 指用各自特有的方式表达心声，强调个人色彩而非音量。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 会一门语言并不等于拥有发言权。（voice n.）
请说出你对这首诗的看法。（voice v.）
每个人都应该在这样的决定上有发言权。（have a voice in）
任何人都不许在课堂上提高嗓门。（raise one's voice）
老师给我们讲了主动语态和被动语态。（voice n.）
那个冬天我因为感冒失声了两次。（lose one's voice）
answers: Knowing a language does not mean having a voice.
Please voice your opinion about the poem.
Everybody should have a voice in decisions like this.
Nobody may raise their voice in class.
The teacher told us about the active and passive voice.
That winter I lost my voice twice because of a cold.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 voice 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: Knowing a language does not mean having a voice, a lesson I learned very slowly.
At first I could not voice an opinion in front of my class, because my own voice sounded strange and thin.
Writing notes at break taught me that most of a good discussion is patient listening.
Our teacher allowed nobody to raise their voice, and later taught us the active and passive voice in grammar.
After losing my voice twice that winter I spoke for one minute in June, in a voice I finally recognised as my own.
Everybody should have a voice in decisions like these, and everyone deserves to be heard in their own voice.
